lx_setup_text: 1. Install Termux from F-Droid (the Google Play build is outdated and unsupported). 2. In Termux run: mkdir -p ~/.termux && echo 'allow-external-apps=true' >> ~/.termux/termux.properties and restart Termux. 3. Grant the launcher the com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND permission: Android Settings → Apps → KateLauncher → Permissions → "Run commands in Termux". 4. Install a Linux distribution in Termux, e.g. pkg install proot-distro && proot-distro install ubuntu (any other way or your own command works too). 5. Disable battery optimization for Termux: Android Settings → Apps → Termux → Battery → Unrestricted. 6. Lift the background process limit (Android 12+), or the system will kill programs in the background: Developer options → "Disable child process restrictions", or via adb: adb shell device_config put activity_manager max_phantom_processes 2147483647. On Android 14+ also: adb shell settings put global settings_enable_monitor_phantom_procs false. 7. For proot-distro the login command must share the Termux temp folder, so the environment can see the launcher's sockets (Wayland and X11): proot-distro login ubuntu --shared-tmp -- 8. X11 mode needs Xwayland in the environment: apt install xwayland. Programs are started with the same commands as in XFCE/X11; the launcher sets DISPLAY (or WAYLAND_DISPLAY in Wayland mode) itself. 9. Then add the environment below, and then your programs. The display mode can be chosen globally, per environment or per program. If a program says it is "already running" or does not react: Session and launching → "Reset session" ends all leftovers in Termux; "Logs…" shows what happened.
lx_add_env_title: Add Linux environment / command that starts the environment via Termux:
lx_howto_text: Add an environment first, then tap + Add program and enter the command that starts the program in that environment's terminal, for example box64 ./app or WINEPREFIX=~/.wine wine app.exe. The command is passed exactly as typed, nothing is parsed or changed. The program then behaves like any other icon (desktop, dock, apps menu, folders).
lx_confirm_env: Delete this environment and all its programs?
lx_app_cmd_hint: Launch command, exactly as typed in the environment terminal
lx_need_fields: Fill in the name and the command
lx_overlay: Windows on top of all apps
lx_overlay_perm: Allow "Display over other apps" for the launcher
lx_saver: Power saving (no transparency or animations, max 30 FPS)
lx_csd_hide: Hide it if the program draws its own
lx_layouts_hint: Zones in percent of the screen: x y w h, separated by ";". Example: 0 0 50 100; 50 0 50 100. Choose a layout from the ▦ button of any window; then drag a window to the top edge and drop it on a zone.
lx_layout_zones: Zones: x y w h; x y w h; ...
lx_layout_bad: Invalid zones (values 0–100, zone must fit the screen)
lw_err_perm: Allow the RUN_COMMAND permission for the launcher (see Linux environments settings)
lw_err_failed: Could not start the command in Termux
lx_sess_off: No session (it starts by itself when you open a Linux program)
lx_display_hint: X11 works like XFCE: programs see a real X11 server (needs the xwayland package in the environment). Wayland uses the native protocol, no Xwayland.
lx_idle: End the session after being idle
lx_reset_confirm: This ends ALL Linux programs and the session itself, including leftovers from crashes (e.g. "Firefox is already running"). Continue?
lx_no_session: No session — no logs or controls yet
lx_err_xwayland_missing: The environment has no Xwayland. Install it: apt install xwayland
lx_err_xwayland_died: Xwayland exited with code %1. See the "Xwayland" log in settings.
lx_err_app_exit: "%1" exited with code %2 without a window. Log: Settings → Linux → Logs.
